title: an array literal of started Promises in an expression statement abandons every Promise it holds
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Promise Semantics': 'Authored `.sm` code MUST consume Promise instances only through `await`.' docs/DECISIONS.md (Locked, Concurrency): every started Promise MUST be consumed. REVIEW-fable-1.md F1 measured this exact program COMPILING, EMITTING AND RUNNING on the Go fork with zero diagnostics: the checked value was discarded at runtime, which is the loss the rule exists to prevent. The fork's unbound must-consume rule fired only when an expression statement's own expression typed as Result or Promise, so every container and operator position was invisible to it. The acceptance direction is 08-promise-chaining/a-bound-promise-array-is-consumed-by-promise-all: an array of started Promises handed to `Promise.all` and awaited is the ordinary concurrent spelling and must stay accepted, so this pair fixes the container rule from both sides.
